investigation,medical	Cardiovascular
Neurological
Both cardiovascular and neurological systems are subjects of medical investigations mentioned in the text.

medical care,referral	People
Specialists
People are advised to be referred to several specialists after investigations.

fitness assessment,provoking factors,restrictions	Driving
Vasovagal Syncope
The condition of vasovagal syncope may require an assessment of fitness to drive depending on the cause and likelihood of recurrence.

assessment criteria,non-benign causes	Cardiovascular Conditions Standards
Vasovagal Syncope
When vasovagal syncope arises from causes other than benign provoking factors, the assessment of fitness to drive follows the cardiovascular conditions standards.

assessment,eligibility,fitness,fitness to drive	Person
Unconditional Licence
A person is determined to be unfit for holding an unconditional licence based on specific medical or diagnostic conditions.<SEP>A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if they have experienced blackouts that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, seizure, or another condition.

driving restriction,medical history	Blackout of Undetermined Nature
Person
A person is prohibited from driving for ten years if they experience two or more blackouts of undetermined nature separated by a 24-hour period.<SEP>A person is prohibited from driving for five years after experiencing a single blackout of undetermined nature.

approval process,authority,evaluation,issuance,licensing decisions,oversight,regulation,review	Conditional Licence
Driver Licensing Authority
The driver licensing authority may consider granting a conditional licence to a person with blackout history subject to annual review and specific criteria.<SEP>The Driver Licensing Authority may consider granting a conditional licence subject to annual reviews.<SEP>The driver licensing authority considers a conditional licence for drivers with blackouts, subject to at least annual review.<SEP>The Driver Licensing Authority makes licensing decisions based on a full consideration of relevant factors relating to health and driving performance.

assessment,consultation,information provision,medical assessment	Appropriate Specialist
Driver Licensing Authority
An appropriate specialist provides information to the driver licensing authority regarding whether a person meets the criterion of having no further blackouts for at least five years.<SEP>An appropriate specialist provides information to the Driver Licensing Authority regarding a person's fitness to drive.

eligibility,time-based criteria	Conditional Licence
Person
A person may be considered for a conditional licence if there have been no further blackouts for at least five years.

health,medical condition	Blackout
Person
A person experiences blackouts of undetermined nature which triggers driving restrictions.

fitness,regulation	Driver Licensing Authority
Unconditional Licence
The Driver Licensing Authority determines if a person is fit to hold an unconditional licence based on blackout history.

diagnosis,exclusion	Person
Syncope
Blackouts that cannot be diagnosed as syncope are considered when assessing a person's fitness to hold an unconditional licence.

diagnosis,exclusion	Person
Seizure
Blackouts that cannot be diagnosed as seizure are considered when assessing a person's fitness to hold an unconditional licence.

process,requirement	Annual Review
Driver Licensing Authority
A conditional licence requires at least annual review by the Driver Licensing Authority.

assessment,driving standards,reference	Figure 6
Person
The standard appropriate to a person's condition is referred to in Figure 6 for managing blackouts related to driving.

assessment,general guidance,reference	Part A section 2
Person
For medical causes of blackouts not covered in specific standards, first principles are referred to in Part A section 2.

data.content:
assessment,reference,uncertain conditions	Person
Table for blackouts of uncertain nature
When a blackout cannot be diagnosed as a covered condition, the table for blackouts of uncertain nature is referenced.

medical care,referral	Cardiovascular and Neurological Investigations
Specialists
Patients undergo cardiovascular and neurological investigations before being referred to specialists.

restriction,safety	Driving
People
Individuals are advised not to engage in driving until medical mechanisms are ascertained and standards are met.

attribution,excuse	Blackout
Drivers
Some drivers attribute a crash or driving mishap to a blackout to excuse an event caused by other reasons.

cause,distraction	Drivers
Inattention
A driving mishap may occur due to inattention rather than a blackout.

cause,mobile phone	Distraction
Drivers
A driving mishap may be caused by distraction, such as engaging in a mobile phone conversation.

familiarisation,requirements	Health professionals
Medical standards for licensing
Health professionals are expected to become acquainted with the outlined medical standards for licensing.

driving,management	Blackouts
Figure 6
The figure provides guidance on managing blackouts in the context of driving safety.

management,medical condition	Figure 6
Syncope
Syncope is listed as a specific medical condition addressed within the figure regarding blackouts and driving.

management,medical condition	Epilepsy/seizure
Figure 6
Epilepsy or seizure is listed as a specific medical condition addressed within the figure regarding blackouts and driving.

management,medical condition	Figure 6
Hypoglycaemic event
A hypoglycaemic event is listed as a specific medical condition addressed within the figure regarding blackouts and driving.

management,medical condition	Drug/alcohol misuse
Figure 6
Drug or alcohol misuse is listed as a specific medical condition addressed within the figure regarding blackouts and driving.

further information,reference	Medical standards for licensing
Section 6.2
The medical standards document references Section 6.2 for additional details.

further information,reference	Figure 6
Section 3
The figure regarding blackouts and driving references Section 3 for related information.

first principles,medical assessment,standards exclusion	Blackout
Fitness to Drive
When a blackout is caused by a medical condition not covered in standards, the assessment of fitness to drive should be conducted using first principles.

driving task nature,risk management,stringent approach	Blackout
Commercial Vehicle Drivers
A more stringent approach regarding blackout recurrence and treatability should be applied for commercial vehicle drivers.

assessment framework,general principles,guidance reference	Fitness to Drive
Part A section 2
The application of first principles regarding fitness to drive refers to the guidance found in Part A section 2.

driving safety,medical evaluation	Blackout of Undetermined Mechanism
Fitness to Drive Assessment
When the mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, fitness to drive should be assessed.

regulatory reference,standards	Fitness to Drive Assessment
Section 1.3 Medical Standards for Licensing
The assessment of fitness to drive is conducted according to the standards found in Section 1.3 Medical Standards for Licensing.

medical comparison,standards	Blackout of Undetermined Mechanism
Seizure
The medical standards applicable to a blackout of undetermined mechanism are similar to those for seizure.

assessment,criteria,exemption	Commercial standards
Conditional licence
A conditional licence may be considered for a person who does not meet commercial standards but is deemed safe by a treating specialist.

opinion,recommendation,safety assessment	Conditional licence
Treating specialist
The treating specialist's opinion determines whether a person with blackouts of undetermined mechanism may be considered safe to drive.

approval,review,risk assessment	Conditional licence
Driver licensing authority
The driver licensing authority considers information from the treating specialist and reviews the risk of a crash caused by a blackout before granting a conditional licence.

conditional licence,heavy vehicle,licensing	Driver Licensing Authority
Farmer
The driver licensing authority considers the nature of the driving task and medical condition when granting a conditional licence to individuals like farmers.

commercial vehicle,interstate,licensing	Driver Licensing Authority
Interstate Multiple Combination Vehicle Driver
The driver licensing authority evaluates the specific driving task and medical condition for drivers of interstate multiple combination vehicles.

advice,examination,medical condition	Driver Licensing Authority
Examining Health Professional
The examining health professional provides advice to the driver licensing authority based on their examination of a person.

driving effects,legal obligation,notification	Driver Licensing Authority
Patient
Patients have a legal obligation to notify the driver licensing authority where their condition affects driving.

medical condition,neurological disorder	Epilepsy
Seizures
Seizures are the primary clinical manifestation associated with the chronic condition known as epilepsy.

causality,medical association	Diabetes mellitus
Vasovagal
Diabetes mellitus is identified as a potential cause or contributing factor for vasovagal episodes.

driving restriction,medical condition,regulation	Blackout
Commercial Standards
The commercial standards define restrictions on driving for individuals who experience blackouts of undetermined nature.

eligibility,fitness,medical criteria	Commercial Standards
Unconditional Licence
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if they have experienced blackouts that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, seizure, or another condition.

eligibility,medical criteria,review	Commercial Standards
Conditional Licence
A conditional licence may be considered by the driver licensing authority for a person who has experienced blackouts, subject to annual review and meeting specific time-based criteria.

assessment,criteria evaluation,medical information	Appropriate Specialist
Conditional Licence
An appropriate specialist provides information to the driver licensing authority regarding whether a driver meets the criterion of having no further blackouts for at least five or ten years.

duration,medical diagnosis,prohibition,recurrence	Blackout
Unconditional Licence
A person should not drive for ten years following two or more blackouts of undetermined nature separated by a twenty-four-hour period.<SEP>A person should not drive for five years following a single blackout of undetermined nature.

eligibility,recurrence,timeframe	Blackout
Conditional Licence
If there has been a single blackout or more than one blackout within a twenty-four-hour period, a conditional licence may be considered if there have been no further blackouts for at least five years.<SEP>If there have been two or more blackouts separated by at least twenty-four hours, a conditional licence may be considered if there have been no further blackouts for at least ten years.

authority,licensing responsibility	Driver Licensing Authority
Person
The Driver Licensing Authority holds ultimate responsibility for issuing, renewing, suspending, or cancelling a person's driver licence.

conditional licence,medical criteria	Driver Licensing Authority
Health Professional
The Health Professional provides details of medical criteria not met, evidence of criteria met, and proposed conditions to the Driver Licensing Authority for a conditional licence.

fitness to drive,medical condition	Concurrent Medical Conditions
Hearing Impairment
Hearing impairment is an example of a medical condition that may combine with other conditions to affect fitness to drive.

fitness to drive,medical condition	Concurrent Medical Conditions
Visual Impairment
Visual impairment is an example of a medical condition that may combine with other conditions to affect fitness to drive.

fitness to drive,medical condition	Cognitive Impairment
Concurrent Medical Conditions
Cognitive impairment is an example of a medical condition that may combine with other conditions to affect fitness to drive.

cause,mechanism,percentage	Blackout
Vasovagal Syncope
Vasovagal syncope is a primary cause of blackouts, accounting for more than 50 per cent of cases.

cardiovascular,cause,mechanism	Blackout
Structural Heart Disease
Structural heart disease is a cardiovascular cause that can lead to syncope and subsequent blackouts.

cardiovascular,cause,mechanism	Arrhythmias
Blackout
Arrhythmias are a type of cardiovascular irregularity that may result in syncope and blackouts.

cardiovascular,cause,mechanism	Blackout
Vascular Disease
Vascular disease is a cardiovascular condition that can cause syncope and blackouts.

cause,mechanism,percentage	Blackout
Epileptic Seizure
Epileptic seizures are a cause of blackouts, accounting for less than 10 per cent of cases.

cause,mechanism,metabolic	Blackout
Hypoglycaemia
Hypoglycaemia is a metabolic cause that can lead to blackouts.

cause,drug-related,mechanism	Blackout
Drug Intoxication
Drug intoxication is a potential cause of blackouts involving the effects of substances.

cause,mechanism,sleep-related	Blackout
Sleep Disorder
Sleep disorders are conditions that may contribute to the occurrence of blackouts.

assessment,determination,method	Blackout
History
History is used as a method to help determine the mechanism of a blackout based on patient background and symptoms.

assessment,determination,method	Blackout
Investigations
Investigations are used as a method to help determine the mechanism of a blackout through medical testing.

assessment,determination,method	Blackout
Specialist Referral
Specialist referral is used as a method to help determine the mechanism of a blackout when initial assessments require further expert evaluation.
